_note: WHICH CAPABILITY CLASSES EACH LEDGER CAPTURE SEAM STRUCTURALLY EXERCISES, AND WHICH IT DOES NOT. This file, not any vector, is what refuses a ledger vector on capability grounds, and it is DATA on purpose: a blind spot discovered later is added here and every affected vector starts being refused with NO vector file changing and no code change. Statuses: exercised (gradeable) | blind (structurally invisible: an implementation honouring it and one ignoring it score identically) | partial (reached, but on a narrower subset than a reader would assume). ONLY 'exercised' permits grading, and an ABSENT entry REFUSES too -- default-deny, DEC-2 §4.10, because an unaudited input is assumed invisible and never assumed wired. THIS IS A SEPARATE FILE FROM capabilities.json AND THAT IS DEC-2 PRECONDITION P-6, DECIDED: capabilities.json's schema id is the hard constant `gerege.loanschedule.capabilities/v1` and its `dec1_revision` is a DEC-1 revision number, so appending ledger rows there would make an amendment of the LOANSCHEDULE contract the thing that re-stamps this context's capability data, and would leave a file whose own schema string names a context half its rows do not belong to. The rejected alternative and the full argument are in nexus/internal/apps/ledger/conformance/capability.go.

capabilities.name: ledger.money.minor.unit.conversion
capabilities.description: The conversion boundary: the reference oracle's MAJOR-unit decimal characters, as emitted on the wire at scale 6, converted to an int64 count of MINOR units by exact integer/string arithmetic, refusing any non-zero digit beyond the currency's minor unit rather than truncating or rounding it.
capabilities.evidence: DEC-2 §4.3, normative consequences 1 and 2, and predicate G-08. EXERCISED AND NON-VACUOUS ONLY SINCE A2-26: before that fire every ledger amount in the A2 corpus was a WHOLE TUGRIK, so a port that dropped or mis-rounded minor units was BYTE-INDISTINGUISHABLE from a correct one on every capture ever taken (DEC-2 §5.0.1). The corpus now carries legs at 270450.580000, 22049.420000, 889549.420000, 20298.820000, 90151.760000, 125000.620000, 25000.370000 and 100000.250000, and the registered wrong implementation `ledger-wrong-truncating` is killed by every one of the four parity vectors. NOTE WHAT IS STILL NOT EXERCISED: no capture carries a NON-ZERO digit beyond two decimal places, so the REFUSAL half of G-08 -- the residue rule -- is specified from source and killed by nothing. A2-8 already stated plainly that no vector proves the truncation rule and that is still true.

capabilities.name: ledger.journal.entry.readback
capabilities.description: A posted journal entry read back at the contract boundary: its legs, each leg's GL account id and code, each leg's DEBIT/CREDIT side, the leg count, and the entry's debit and credit totals.
capabilities.evidence: Exercised by GET /journalentries (A2-338, A2-347, A2-383) and by the ledger_db_readback seam (A2-390). THE CELL THIS DELIBERATELY EXCLUDES is glAccountType: A2-26 observed the identical row rendering ASSET in A2-088 and INCOME in A2-320, every other cell byte-identical, with NO entry edited, because the field projects the ACCOUNT'S CURRENT classification rather than the entry's and GL account 2 was retyped underneath five live product mappings (G-10). So NO VECTOR IN THIS STORE GRADES A GL ACCOUNT'S CLASSIFICATION, and a port that resolves an entry's classification wrongly is not caught here.

PRODUCTS 22, 23, 24, 27 AND 28 ARE INADMISSIBLE and the pin denylists them: A2-26 re-sent each of their mappings (A2-300..A2-315) and the oracle returned 403 on every one. capabilities.name: ledger.refusal.parity
capabilities.description: An ORACLE-OBSERVED refusal: the HTTP status, the oracle's own globalisation code and its message text, as returned on the wire and captured.
capabilities.evidence: Exercised by A2-344 and A2-346, both HTTP 403 with distinct globalisation codes. It is graded on all THREE cells because a port returning 403 with an invented code is not matching the oracle. A THIRD REFUSAL JOINED THEM: T294's OB-01, HTTP 403 error.msg.journalentry.defining.openingbalance.not.allowed, promoted as LDG-REFUSE-03 -- and it is the first refusal in this corpus whose PRECEDENCE is observed rather than asserted, because OB-01's body was unbalanced by one minor unit and the oracle answered with the opening-balance code, so :717 is measured to beat the balance check at :651. [UPDATED by T295: the population is now FIVE.] The two date refusals of validateBusinessRulesForJournalEntries are NO LONGER UNCOVERED. LDG-REFUSE-04 promotes T287's A2-01 -- an entry dated ON the latest closing date, HTTP 403 error.msg.glJournalEntry.invalid.accounting.closed -- and LDG-REFUSE-05 promotes T287's A1-02 -- an entry dated one day after the business date, HTTP 403 error.msg.glJournalEntry.invalid.future.date. Both are PROMOTIONS OF BYTES ALREADY ON DISK: neither probe was re-fired, and neither may be, because both bodies are valid, balanced, postable manual journal entries whose only defect is an ORACLE-SIDE precondition that has lapsed (T287 deleted the closure) or lapses imminently (the calendar). [CORRECTED BY T328, AND THE SENTENCE IT REPLACES IS QUOTED SO THE CORRECTION CAN BE FOUND FROM IT.] This row used to end: "only the REFUSAL side of each boundary is pinned. That an entry dated closingDate + 1 day, or one dated ON the business date, is ACCEPTED with HTTP 200 is [UNVERIFIED] in this store ... Both are filed as backlog ... (B-1, B-2) and NEITHER WAS FIRED." EVERY CLAUSE OF THAT IS NOW FALSE. T327 FIRED BOTH ARMS on a throwaway instance and BOTH RETURNED HTTP 200 [VERIFIED: .softhouse/capture/t327-closure-accepting-side/throwaway/out/B1-ACCEPT-06-entry-one-day-after-closing-date.status and B2-ACCEPT-01-entry-on-business-date.status], and T328 PROMOTED BOTH as LDG-06-postclosure-entry-accepted-one-day-after-closing-date and LDG-07-entry-on-the-business-date-accepted. The reason the old sentence gave -- "capturing an acceptance means POSTING A JOURNAL ENTRY THAT CANNOT BE DELETED" -- was TRUE AND NOT AN OBSTACLE: a journal entry still cannot be deleted, but an INSTANCE can, and the standing reference oracle was never written to (its seven counters are byte-identical before, during and after). WHAT THIS MEANS FOR THIS ROW SPECIFICALLY: the refusal population is STILL FIVE and this row still covers refusals only -- LDG-06 and LDG-07 are PARITY vectors and claim ledger.journal.entry.readback, ledger.money.minor.unit.conversion, ledger.manual.entry.posting and ledger.opening.balance.and.closure, NOT this row. The correction here is not a count change; it is that this row may no longer be read as evidence that the accepting side is unobserved. WHAT IS STILL NOT COVERED BY THIS ROW, restated so the next reader does not over-read it: every refusal it names is a refusal SHAPE the oracle produced, and no vector in this store grades the refusal PRECEDENCE between the two date rules -- :630 runs before :636 [JournalEntryWritePlatformServiceJpaRepositoryImpl.java:626-640] and no capture sends a request that violates BOTH, so a port that evaluates them in either order scores identically. ledger-wrong-date-rules-always-refusing consults them in the INVERTED order and dies on neither refusal vector for that reason [MEASURED: .softhouse/capture/t328-date-rule-promotion/out/20-mutation-arms.txt, arm W-1 vs W-2].

capabilities.name: ledger.slot.resolution
capabilities.description: Resolving a loan product's placeholder slot to a GL account through acc_product_mapping, including the payment-type precedence chain and the cash/accrual family selection.
capabilities.evidence: NOT GRADED BY ANY VECTOR IN THIS STORE. The four parity vectors assert a journal ENTRY read back from the oracle; none of them asserts that a (product, slot, payment type) triple resolves to a particular account. The resolver exists in the Go port (Resolver.ResolveLoanProductAccount) and A2-8 graded resolution against the product read-back, but that grading was never promoted into a vector and this task did not promote it either: doing so needs a request shape whose slot_code names ONE slot, and every entry in the multi-leg corpus spans several. Marked false so that a vector claiming this capability is REFUSED rather than graded against nothing.

capabilities.name: ledger.accrual.entry
capabilities.description: An accrual journal entry -- INTEREST_RECEIVABLE, FEES_RECEIVABLE or PENALTIES_RECEIVABLE.
capabilities.evidence: ENTIRELY UNGRADED, and the reason is that the observations do not exist rather than that the machinery does not. Product 28 is the only ACCRUAL_PERIODIC product (m_product_loan.accounting_type = 3, and it is the ONLY row with that value), it HAS NO LOAN (m_loan carries no product_id = 28; loans 1-7 are on products 22, 22, 27, 24, 46, 46, 55), and no accrual or COB job has ever run -- so NOT ONE JOURNAL ENTRY IN THIS TENANT ARRIVED THROUGH A RECEIVABLE SLOT. Product 28's own mapping is inadmissible today (A2-314, 403). An accrual vector needs a NEW accrual product on clean accounts PLUS a job run; neither is in this task's scope and neither is cheap. THE CLAIM IS ABOUT THE SLOTS, NOT THE ACCOUNTS, and unposted_slots below records them as structured data so the harness can decode each slot name through the ported AccrualAccountsForLoan enum and MEASURE each backing account's activity against the promoted corpus on every run. [CORRECTED by T242, A2-34 F-4. This row used to assert 'gl 18, 22 and 16 carry ZERO journal entries' and the harness printed that sentence on every run, pass or fail, as a measured fact. Re-derived against the live PostgreSQL reference oracle: gl 18 -> 0, gl 22 -> 0, gl 16 -> SIXTEEN, the most of any account in the ledger, and gl 16 is a promoted leg of LDG-01, LDG-02 and LDG-03. The error was structural rather than clerical: ONE GL ACCOUNT BACKS SEVERAL SLOTS. gl 16 is PENALTIES_RECEIVABLE (slot 9) on product 28 AND FUND_SOURCE (slot 1) on products 22, 27, 46, 54 and 55, and all sixteen of its rows arrive through the latter. The slot is unposted; the account is not empty.]

THE BUSINESS DATE IS MEASURED, NOT DERIVED, which is a strictly better provenance than LDG-REFUSE-04 and LDG-REFUSE-05 have: /businessdates returned 404 on that instance, so it was BRACKETED -- accepted at 2026-08-28, refused at 2026-08-29 with error.msg.glJournalEntry.invalid.future.date -- and the builder recomputes the bracket from the committed bytes and refuses to emit if it does not close. THE ZONE IS OBSERVED, NOT CONFIGURED: the run landed at 17:33Z, the one hour where UTC read 2026-08-27 and Asia/Ulaanbaatar read 2026-08-28, so an instance reading the business date in UTC would have REFUSED LDG-07's arm. It accepted. WHERE IT WAS TAKEN: the same throwaway pattern T305 established, tenant `t327` at Asia/Ulaanbaatar and rounding-mode 4 (HALF_UP), same docker image as the standing oracle, destroyed in the same run, and the standing oracle's seven counters identical before, during and after. WHAT IS STILL NOT GRADED ON THIS ROW AFTER T328: the two REVERSAL items above are untouched, T296's ARM B is still unkilled, and the refusal PRECEDENCE between :630 and :636 is graded by nothing -- no capture sends a request that violates both date rules, so a port evaluating them in either order scores identically. THE DATE FIELDS THE ORACLE RETURNS ARE DELIBERATELY UNGRADED: /journalentries createdDate is a plain ALIAS for submittedOnDate [JournalEntryData.java:63, :211; the read query has no created-date column] and is the WALL-CLOCK tenant day at insertion, so grading it as a literal would make a parity vector pass or fail on what time of day CI ran -- T327's own capture shows /glclosures reporting createdDate '2026-08-27' (JVM/UTC day) and /journalentries reporting [2026,8,28] (tenant business day) AT THE SAME INSTANT. Both promoted vectors are built from the DATABASE readback, which has no such column [T329].

capabilities.name: ledger.reversal.entry
capabilities.description: A correction posted as a reversing entry (I-5).
capabilities.evidence: A REVERSAL NOW EXISTS IN THE CORPUS -- A2-348 reversed transaction a28f573f34c7 and A2-349 read the three legs back carrying reversed = true -- which CORRECTS DEC-2 §4.4's stated reason ('the A2 corpus contains no reversal'), written before that capture was taken. What is still missing is the other half of I-5's statement: 'a correction ADDS a leg pair; it never MUTATES one'. The read-back shows the reversed FLAG SET on the original rows, and distinguishing 'flags and adds' from 'flags and rewrites' needs the WRITE path, not a snapshot. So this stays out of the graded domain with a corrected reason, and no reversal vector is promoted.
